column3: “Will take” supplies a separate action before the judgment carried out with the sword.
“Fruitful” renders the description of the vineyard as delightful.
“Trample them” adds an action to marching against the thorns; “to the ground” expands burning them together.
“The LORD” and “Israel” name the agents and object that the Hebrew expresses by pronouns.
“Warfare and exile” renders the language of measure and sending away; the Hebrew shifts from “You contend” to “He drove out.”
“Calves” is a single calf in the Hebrew.
“Euphrates” identifies what the Hebrew calls “the River.”
